_about: Step 2 functional-role classifier rules. All patterns are case-insensitive substring matches; no specific part numbers — only protocol conventions and KiCad library family names. Add a pattern to a list and ALL future ICs in that family classify correctly without code changes.

role_priority._comment: Tie-break order when a node has equal vote counts for multiple roles. Earlier = higher priority. MAIN_CONTROLLER is assigned separately by score, not by votes, so it does not appear here.

main_controller._comment: Picked by graph-importance score AFTER role classification (so a node already labeled POWER_REGULATOR cannot become MAIN_CONTROLLER even if it scored highest). The single highest-scoring node that meets ALL these thresholds AND whose current role is NOT in excluded_roles wins MAIN_CONTROLLER. If no candidate qualifies (e.g. a power-only sheet with only buck converters and protection), main_controller is None — which is correct, those sheets don't have a central controller.

net_patterns._comment: Net-name substring -> role vote. Most reliable signal — protocol nets are universal conventions and reveal exactly what each component does. A 0.1uF cap between MCU.NRST and GND will see net 'NRST' and correctly classify as RESET. Substrings match anywhere in the net name unless prefixed with ^ (then it's a prefix match).

lib_id_patterns._comment: lib_id substring -> role vote. Family-level KiCad library names only — these are NOT circuit-specific (Crystal applies to any Y_*, Connector applies to any J_*, Diode_TVS applies to any TVS part). Adding a part number here would violate the no-hardcode rule; add the family instead.

refdes_patterns._comment: Refdes-prefix -> role. Used as last-resort family hint when lib_id and net patterns don't decide. Longest-prefix wins. Passives (R/C) get GENERIC because their actual role depends on the net they sit on (decoupling cap belongs to POWER, NRST cap to RESET, etc.) — the net_patterns above pull them into the right block when applicable; for unconnected passives GENERIC is correct.

value_patterns._comment: Component value-field substring -> role vote. Useful for passives whose value field carries family info (TVS array values, ferrite-bead part codes).

value_regex_patterns._comment: Component value-field regex -> role. Higher specificity than substring matches (the substring table above stays as a fallback). Patterns are case-insensitive. Order matters when a value matches multiple roles — first hit wins.

pin_geometry_rules._comment: Ordered list of pin-geometry rules. First match wins. min_pins/max_pins bracket the pin count, requires_power gates on the node touching at least one power rail (filters out unconnected ICs), refdes_prefix narrows the rule to a refdes family. Conservative on purpose — a 2-pin body could be R/C/L/D, so the only 2-pin rule is the geometry-only path that lands all of them in GENERIC and lets value_regex carry the protection diodes back to PROTECTION.

trust_layers._comment: Trust-based 4-layer classifier. Highest trust layer's role wins; ties break by total agreement across layers, then by role_priority. Nodes whose top-layer trust falls below fallback_threshold get role=GENERIC and llm_candidate=true — the LLM fallback path then targets only those nodes, not the whole sheet. Set enabled=false to revert to the legacy vote-sum classifier.

power_only_fallback._comment: If a node has zero non-power signal edges but DOES touch one or more power rails, classify as POWER (typical for bulk caps and decoupling caps). Without this they would land in GENERIC.

llm._comment: LLM fallback for nodes the heuristic landed in GENERIC (or, with reclassify_all, every node). One batched Claude call per render — see llm_classifier.py. role_allowlist constrains the model's vocabulary so it can't invent new roles. min_pin_count filters out passives where the heuristic is already authoritative.
